answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy uses identity-bound sequential attestation chains that start at dawn of registration. Each identity must complete a non-parallelizable sequence of peer-verified tasks whose history is non-transferable. An attacker running n clones pays n times the elapsed real-time cost, since no clone can inherit another's progress. At the nadir of any identity's score after a break, weight collapses and the full sequence restarts. Velvet allows only short legitimate pauses without reset, so splitting still multiplies the scarce time resource.
